title: 2025 single, itemized $17,000 against standard $15,750: itemizes, and there is no non-itemizer gift deduction to add

source.where: 26 USC 170(p) and (b)(1)(I) start with taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025 (Pub. L. 119-21 sections 70424 to 70429); Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 3.01: standard deduction $15,750

note: 2025 has no 0.5% floor, so the whole $1,000 of gifts counts when itemizing: 16,000 + 1,000 = 17,000, over the standard 15,750 (and no gift is added to the standard path in 2025). Taxable 100,000 - 17,000 = 83,000.

title: 2025 single, age 64 at year end, born January 1, 1961: the extra standard deduction counts

source.where: Publication 501 (2025), Higher Standard Deduction for Age: you are considered 65 on the day before your 65th birthday, so for 2025 if you were born before January 2, 1961

title: 2025 single, age 64 at year end, born January 2, 1961: no extra standard deduction

source.where: Publication 501 (2025), Higher Standard Deduction for Age: born before January 2, 1961 is 65 or older at the end of 2025

note: Born January 2, 1961 is not before January 2, 1961: 15,750.

title: 2025 single, $40,000 of mortgage interest on a $1,000,000 loan: $30,000 counts

source.where: Publication 936 (2025), Reminders and the Part II worksheet line 8: $750,000 ($375,000 if married filing separately) of indebtedness

note: 750,000 / 1,000,000 = 75% of the 40,000 = 30,000 (the share of the loan under the limit; Pub. 936 gives the limit, the proration is by the average balance). Taxable 300,000 - 30,000 = 270,000.
